text: dsh-router-flash 是面向 DSH 网页端的 agent preset，通过模型 ID 和首条用户消息选择引导方式。它在提示词组装时替换 persona；DeepSeek Flash 使用专属弱引导，其他模型按家族及 build/fix 关键词分类。对于支持的模型，首次工具调用前仅开放核心文件工具和平台 shell，工具结果返回后恢复完整工具目录；第三方模型不收窄工具。它还可依据工具执行收据推进预先声明的确定性动作链，条件不满足时停止推进。适合希望按模型调整提示词与首轮工具范围的 DSH 用户；代码未读取到需要配置 API key 或外部服务。

dsh-router-flash routes a DSH agent preset by model and task. It selects a persona during prompt assembly and limits supported models to core tools for the first turn, restoring the catalog after a tool result. Third-party models keep the full tool set. Guarded receipts advance action chains.

dsh-router-flash 的功能「按模型选择 persona」：提示词组装时读取模型 ID 和首条用户消息，为 DeepSeek Flash、其他 DeepSeek、LongCat 和第三方模型选择相应引导。
dsh-router-flash 的功能「首轮核心工具限制」：为非第三方模型按任务模式开放核心文件工具，并补充 bash 或 pwsh；首次工具结果后解除限制。
dsh-router-flash 的功能「任务关键词分类」：读取首条用户消息，按 build/create 与 fix/debug 等关键词计数，选择 react、spec 或 weak 模式。
dsh-router-flash 的功能「收据条件动作链」：对工具结果检查退出码、输出文本、状态或 JSON 条件；满足时调度下一项预先声明的动作，不满足则清空队列。

dsh-router-flash README · HarnessMM 决策重用（GDR / CCS）：`lib/router-core.mjs` 带一层来自 [HarnessMM](https://github.com/YuhuaJiang2002/HarnessMM)（Apache-2.0）
的确定性决策重用逻辑。模型可以在一次慢思考里声明一小串确定性后续动作，控制器在
本地连续置换执行，只要每一步的卫述被上一步的收据满足——不必再调一次模型。

dsh-router-flash README · HarnessMM 决策重用（GDR / CCS）：| 导出 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `evaluateGuard(guard, receipt)` | 用卫述条件评估工具收据：`return_code` / `exitCode`、`stdout_contains`、`stdout_equals`、`stderr_empty`、`json_equals`、`status == success` |
| `shouldBypassCallback(receipt, candidate)` | 候选动作的卫述被满足且参数完整（字面闭合）时为真 |
| `ChiselPlanScheduler` | 每会话的候选节点队列；`step(receipt)` 推进并返回下一个动作，卫述不满足时返回 `null`（安全回退给模型） |
| `createSubstitutionCertificate(meta)` | 为被置换掉的慢思考调用留审计凭证 |
| `isRedundantVerification(prevReceipt, currentAction)` | 幂等拦截：上一步测试已通过时，抑制重复跑同一个测试 |

dsh-router-flash README · HarnessMM 决策重用（GDR / CCS）：接线在 `lib/router-bootstrap.mjs`：`agent/created` 登记首轮 `tools.restrict()`；
`tools/result` 解除收窄并把收据喂给调度器。队列由模型自己声明的候选填充——preset
不发明动作。卫述失败时队列清空，控制权交还模型的正常推理。

这段逻辑是 `LICENSE` / `NOTICE` 里 Apache-2.0 例外的同一部分，见「致谢与来源」。

  家族的习惯，不是安全或测量结论。
- 本 preset 保持 `false`（跟随家族）。要开启：把该行的 `fetch` 改成 `true`，并同步改

dsh-router-flash README · 适用范围：- 命中 `isFlashModel` 后一律走 weak 模式（作者实测 w7 最优解）。

- HarnessMM 决策重用层对所有家族生效：模型可以声明一小串确定性链条，控制器在

dsh-router-flash README · What it is：A dsh **agent preset** delivered as a bundle patch layer. Installing the
plugin declares one `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row; restart dsh and
「探索模式」 appears in the preset picker. **Nothing is written to disk** — since
DSH 0.2.0 the preset is a plugin row, not a directory.

What it does:

dsh-router-flash README · What it is：| Stage | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Match** | `isFlashModel(id) = /deepseek/i.test(id) && /flash/i.test(id)` — model- and channel-agnostic; `modelFamily()` splits ids into `flash` / `deepseek` / `longcat` / `third-party` |
| **Persona** | For Flash, always the weak branch (w7 guidance): classify, review, stay on topic, think deeply, close the loop |
| **First turn** | Only `read` / `write` / `edit` plus the platform shell (`bash`, or `pwsh` on Windows) |
| **After the first `tool/call`** | The full 28-row catalog opens; the router also runs the HarnessMM chained bypass on `tools/result` |

dsh-router-flash README · What it is：The router hooks the `system-prompt/assemble` seam for persona routing. On
DSH 0.2.2+ the first-turn narrowing is registered via `ctx.tools.restrict()`
on `agent/created` and lifted on the first `tools/result`; on older hosts the
assemble payload still carries `tools` and the filter runs there. Mode derives
from durable session events, so resume/reload keeps it.

dsh-router-flash README · Model-agnostic by design：This preset is the evolved branch of the earlier `dsh-router-flash` (v0.1.0,
which was bound to a single provider's DeepSeek V4 Flash). The routing was
rebuilt so the preset is **not tied to one vendor or model family**:

dsh-router-flash README · Model-agnostic by design：- **Any channel** — the match is on the model id, not on who resells it. Any
  provider serving DeepSeek V4 Flash gets the same guidance.
- **Any model, but not the same guidance** — ids map to four families:
  `flash` (DeepSeek + flash) gets w7 plus first-turn narrowing; other DeepSeek
  models get w6 keyword classification plus narrowing; `longcat` gets its own
  long-context persona plus narrowing; `third-party` models (gemini, qwen,
  gpt, …) no longer narrow the first turn, while their persona still follows
  keyword classification by default (neutral is opt-in).
- **One preset, many models** — the same declaration row serves every model;
  the router adapts per session instead of needing a preset per vendor.

dsh-router-flash README · Model-agnostic by design：This is the extensibility gain: adding a new model or channel needs no preset
change — only the model id and (for routing) the provider config.

dsh-router-flash README · Match rule (model- and channel-agnostic)：```
isFlashModel(modelId) = /deepseek/i.test(modelId) && /flash/i.test(modelId)
```

`modelFamily()` reads the id only:

dsh-router-flash README · Match rule (model- and channel-agnostic)：| Model id | Family | Route |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` | `flash` | w7 guidance + first-turn narrowing (this preset's main path) |
| `deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-chat` | `deepseek` | keyword classification of the first user message (build/fix) + first-turn narrowing |
| `LongCat-*`, `longcat-*` | `longcat` | long-context persona (`WEAK_LONGCAT`) + first-turn narrowing |
| `gemini-2.5-flash`, `qwen3-flash`, `gpt-5-flash` | `third-party` | keyword classification by default, neutral opt-in; **no first-turn narrowing** |

dsh-router-flash README · Match rule (model- and channel-agnostic)：**Only one third-party behaviour changed, because only one was measured**: the
narrowed first turn kept the prompt explaining `glob`/`grep` while the schema
carried neither. That mismatch reproduced in **13 of 13** historical
third-party sessions on this machine (`scripts/replay-routing.mjs` replays
them), so third-party models now always get the full catalog. The persona is
untouched: w6 and w7 were measured only on DeepSeek models, so the default
stays `classify`; `thirdPartyGuidance: neutral` is available for a measured
A/B, not as a new default.

dsh-router-flash README · Match rule (model- and channel-agnostic)：**Why not match `flash` alone**: that would drag non-DeepSeek models
(`gemini-2.5-flash`, `qwen3-flash`) into this preset's weak persona, which is a
negative optimisation for them.

**Why not bind to `opencode-go`**: a model's capability comes from the model,
not from who resells it. Any channel's DeepSeek V4 Flash should get the same
guidance; channel differences belong in the `provider` config, not the preset.

dsh-router-flash README · HarnessMM decision reuse (GDR / CCS)：`lib/router-core.mjs` carries a deterministic decision-reuse layer derived from
[HarnessMM](https://github.com/YuhuaJiang2002/HarnessMM) (Apache-2.0). It lets
the model declare a short chain of deterministic follow-up actions in one slow
thinking pass, and the controller executes them locally without another model
call — as long as each step's guard is satisfied by the previous step's receipt.

dsh-router-flash README · HarnessMM decision reuse (GDR / CCS)：| Export | Role |
|---|---|
| `evaluateGuard(guard, receipt)` | Evaluates a tool receipt against a guard: `return_code` / `exitCode`, `stdout_contains`, `stdout_equals`, `stderr_empty`, `json_equals`, `status == success` |
| `shouldBypassCallback(receipt, candidate)` | True when a candidate action's guard is satisfied and its args are complete (literal closure) |
| `ChiselPlanScheduler` | Per-session queue of candidate nodes; `step(receipt)` advances and returns the next action, or `null` when the guard fails (safe fallback to the model) |
| `createSubstitutionCertificate(meta)` | Audit record for a bypassed slow-thinking call |
| `isRedundantVerification(prevReceipt, currentAction)` | Idempotence guard: suppresses re-running an already-passed test command |

dsh-router-flash README · HarnessMM decision reuse (GDR / CCS)：The wiring lives in `lib/router-bootstrap.mjs`: `agent/created` registers the
first-turn `tools.restrict()`; `tools/result` lifts the restriction and feeds
the receipt to the scheduler. The scheduler's queue is populated by the model's
own declared candidates — the preset does not invent actions. When a guard
fails, the queue is cleared and control returns to the model's normal reasoning.

dsh-router-flash README · HarnessMM decision reuse (GDR / CCS)：This is the same logic that carries the Apache-2.0 notice in `LICENSE` /
`NOTICE`; see 「Credits and provenance」.

dsh-router-flash README · Runtime robustness：- **No more disk writes**: since 0.4.0 the preset is delivered by the
  composition layer. At startup the plugin does one read-only check (is the
  old `.agent-presets/router-flash` still there) and degrades that single
  thing's failure to a log line — an explanatory plugin must never keep the
  host from booting.
- **A missing shell is no longer fatal**: when the tool catalog has neither
  `bash` nor `pwsh`, the first turn degrades to file tools and logs a warning
  instead of throwing and failing the whole request.
- **A narrower crash surface**: the routing logic depends on only four seams
  (the `system-prompt/assemble` event, the `agent/created` event, the
  `tools/result` event, session events); if any seam changes it degrades or
  warns, and never throws through to the whole request.

dsh-router-flash README · What was adapted (relative to upstream v0.1.0)：Upstream relied on three mechanisms that were already dead on `0.1.0-rc.6`;
this preset carries over its fixes and adds the 0.1.5 adaptation:

1. `ctx.on('session/event')` injection — session/event is session-scoped, so
   an agent-plane preset never receives it.
2. `target.inbox.append` — the agent object has no `.inbox` property.
3. At assembly time there is no user/message in the events yet — a timing
   problem.

dsh-router-flash README · Scope：- Once `isFlashModel` matches, it always takes the weak branch (the author's
  measured optimum, w7).
- Non-Flash DeepSeek models (e.g. `deepseek-v4-pro`) take the keyword
  classification path and can still use the preset.
- Third-party models (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash`) keep keyword
  classification by default but no longer narrow the first turn; the neutral
  sentence is opt-in via `thirdPartyGuidance: neutral`. LongCat ids form their
  own `longcat` family with a dedicated long-context persona.
- Complex build tasks (large projects, greenfield development) benefit most
  from the deep-thinking anchor.
- The HarnessMM decision-reuse layer applies to every family: the model can
  declare a short deterministic chain and the controller executes it locally
  while each guard holds, falling back to normal reasoning the moment one
  fails.

dsh-router-flash README · Notes：- The host plugin **no longer writes to disk**. 0.3.x used Node's native file
  API to sync the preset directory (to dodge startup ordering); as of 0.4.0
  that entire write path is gone — the preset goes through the composition
  layer and the plugin is left with one read-only check.
- Override the preset by Loader row id (`preset-router-flash`) in the
  profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, replacing the whole `config`; **an override is
  a whole-value replacement, so omitting a field loses it** — restate `id` /
  `plugins` when overriding.
- The row id `preset-router-flash` is the Loader address; `config.id:
  router-flash` is the identity a session remembers. Renaming it would make
  old sessions lose their preset, so it is fixed.
